introduction.en: The World Health Organization (WHO) is the specialized UN agency responsible for international public health. It serves as the directing and coordinating authority on global health matters.
introduction.hi: The World Health Organization (WHO) is the specialized UN agency responsible for international public health. It serves as the directing and coordinating authority on global health matters.

body.en: The WHO enhances global health security through the International Health Regulations (IHR), which mandate the reporting of public health emergencies. For India, a robust health system is critical for economic growth, as health is a key component of human capital. WHO's technical guidance helps India in disease control, immunization, and building resilient health systems, which directly reduces the economic burden of diseases and improves labor productivity.

conclusion.en: While the WHO faces challenges in funding and governance, its role remains indispensable. India must continue to engage with the WHO to align domestic health policies with global best practices.

overview.title: World Health Organization
overview.definition: The World Health Organization (WHO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health, established on 7 April 1948 with its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC Prelims (International Organizations, health indices, funding mechanisms, statutory conventions) and Mains GS Paper II (Global governance, multilateral bodies, health diplomacy, and pandemic management).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of World Health Organization.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of international relations and global health governance

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The WHO Constitution came into force on **World Health Day** (7 April 1948), defining health not merely as the absence of disease, but as a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: The organization operates under the supreme authority of the **World Health Assembly (WHA)**, comprising delegates from all 194 member states, which determines organization policies and appoints the Director-General.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: Executive governance is managed by the **Executive Board**, consisting of 34 technically qualified members elected for three-year terms to give effect to WHA decisions.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: WHO funding comprises **Assessed Contributions** (mandatory dues from member states) and **Voluntary Contributions** (earmarked funds from member states and philanthropic bodies like the Gates Foundation).

items.definition: A legally binding instrument of international law that creates rights and obligations for countries to report public health events of international concern (PHEIC).

items.term: Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC)
items.definition: An extraordinary event formally declared by the WHO Director-General that constitutes a public health risk to other states through the international spread of disease.
Co-led by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), Gavi, and WHO, designed to ensure equitable global access to COVID-19 vaccines.
Global Action Plan for Healthy Lives and Well-being for All; Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) - WHO's first treaty negotiated under Article 19.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Regional Office for South-East Asia (SEARO)**: Headquartered in New Delhi, India, coordinating public health policies for 11 member states.
• **Driving Advantages**: Strategic positioning for tackling tropical diseases, polio eradication milestones, and Universal Health Coverage (UHC) frameworks across developing economies.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Heavy reliance on voluntary earmarked funding leads to donor-driven priorities; perceived bureaucratic delays and geopolitical pressures during global health crises.
• **Policy Interventions**: Proposals for sustainable financing, strengthening the Pandemic Treaty negotiations, and establishing the WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence in Berlin.

items.title: Mnemonic for WHO Regional Offices
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'PASEWE' (Panama And South East West Europe)
• **Decoded Meaning**: Pan American (AMRO), Africa (AFRO), South-East Asia (SEARO), Eastern Mediterranean (EMRO), Western Pacific (WPRO), Europe (EURO).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly rules out non-WHO regional bodies or incorrect headquarters locations in matching lists.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: WHO is a specialized UN agency (established 1948, Geneva) – remember that unlike the World Bank, it does not provide structural adjustment loans but normative guidance and technical assistance.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that WHO has the power to mandate lockdowns or enforce border closures globally. Remember that WHO can only issue 'recommendations' under IHR 2005; sovereign states retain final legal authority over national borders and domestic laws.

Mains Value Addition: In answers concerning global health security or post-COVID recovery, quote the necessity of reforming the WHO through sustainable core funding and strengthening the legally binding Pandemic Agreement.

keyTakeaways: WHO is a specialized UN agency established in 1948 with headquarters in Geneva and six autonomous regional offices, including SEARO in New Delhi.
The World Health Assembly is the supreme decision-making body, while the Executive Board manages technical execution.
International Health Regulations (IHR 2005) provide the legal framework for declaring a PHEIC, though enforcement relies entirely on member-state sovereignty.
